meta.purpose: live measurement of what consuming N USES of a food does to it -- the rule data/recipes.json's nutrition deltas rest on (06-recipes/q-itemcount-notes.md, Open #1)
meta.rule: every field multiplyFoodValues writes is scaled by (1 - used/currentUses), used = min(getCurrentUses(), requested); maxUses and baseHunger do not move
meta.foods_use: the per-item script macros the spawn_guard block checks the spawned instance against; every scaling expectation is built from the LIVE before snapshot, not from this file

tolerance.why: Food is float32 and TK.json rounds to 6 decimals; the relative term is the brief's 1e-4

meta.world_changes: none -- no settimespeed, no sandbox write, no character write. The spawned items live in this run's COPY of the fixture.

icecream_third.note: 10 of 30 uses -- a THIRD of a tub, ScoopIceCream's own `item 10 [Base.Icecream]` line. The only row whose factor is neither 0 nor 1, so it is the one that separates `1 - used/currentUses` from `one use = one item` and from `N is a count of items`. Predicted -0.30 -> -0.20 and 1680 -> 1120 kcal
icecream_third.pre_existing: no item Base.Icecream in admin's inventory

use.predictedFactorBasis: multiplyFoodValues(1 - used/currentUses), via Food.setCurrentUses -> consumeHunger; equal to 1 - used/maxUses only while the item is whole
use.route: item:setCurrentUses(20)  [= ItemUser.UseItem @28 L37-38, without its RemoveItem]

current_uses_is_whole.basis: a freshly spawned item must be whole, and only then is maxUses the scaling denominator

in_container.basis: the spawned item is in the player's inventory before the call

instances_before.basis: exactly one instance of this type in the inventory when the command ran

currentUses.basis: Food.getCurrentUses = (int)|hungChange * 100| @14-@26 L2219-L2223; band is one truncation unit

max_uses_unmoved.basis: multiplyFoodValues never touches baseHunger, so getMaxUses() must not move -- this is what makes currentUses, not maxUses, the denominator of any SECOND reduction

base_hunger_unmoved.basis: the same claim read off the float rather than the int

current_uses_after.basis: a partial consumption must leave uses above 0

removed_from_inventory.basis: ItemUser.UseItem @272 L68-70 removes a depleted item; the setCurrentUses fallback is the reduction line only, so on that route a depleted item is expected to STAY -- expectation computed for the route that ran (item:setCurrentUses(20)  [= ItemUser.UseItem @28 L37-38, wit)

still_in_container.basis: InventoryItem.getContainer() != null, the same claim read off the item instead of the inventory

item_get_before_found.basis: the RCON spawn is keyed on item.get, not on the RCON reply (which is empty on success)

same_instance_before.basis: item.get's getFirstTypeRecurse vs item.use's fullest-then-newest pick -- with one instance in the inventory (spawn_guard.instances_before) the two cannot disagree

item_get_after_found.basis: a removed item is no longer findable; on the setCurrentUses route it still is

hungChange.basis: the same field read by a second server command

calories.basis: the same field read by a second server command

carbs.basis: the same field read by a second server command

lipids.basis: the same field read by a second server command

proteins.basis: the same field read by a second server command

factor.basis: multiplyFoodValues(1 - used/currentUses); the compared expectations use the float32 value

atomic_window_game_hours.basis: before/after are taken on either side of the single setter INSIDE one command handler. Band 1e-5 game-hours = 0.036 game-seconds, far below one tick; TK.json rounds to 6 decimals so anything under 5e-7 reads back as exactly 0

thirstChange.why: multiplyFoodValues @42 L2292 scales getThirstChangeUnmodified() while TK.ITEM_STATE reads the MODIFIED getter -- not the same number, so comparing them would be a defect in this script, not a finding

hungerChange.why: the read-time getter that applies the cooked/burnt/stale ladder (02-notes Q3); recorded so `hungChange` moving while this does not (or vice versa) is visible
